decisions.statement: The slug this module is handed is one already held to lower kebab case.
A `-` a lowercase ascii letter or an ascii digit follows is dropped and that character is raised.
A `-` anything else follows stays where it is.
A letter outside ascii is kept as the slug spells it.
The type a page type declares is that name with its first character raised.
A slug that cannot become a page's export name is answered here with why.
A name opening with a digit is no identifier.
The slug making such a name is at fault.
A name TypeScript keeps for itself is at fault though that name is an identifier.
A word reserved only under strict mode is kept too.
The fault is said as the name the slug makes rather than as the slug.
Nothing here loads a module or reads the disk.
Nothing here reaches a page or an index or a change.
Nothing here folds a key that is no slug.

definition: the names a page's slug makes, for the value it is bound to and for the type it is
